description.value: The study investigated whether fMRI neurofeedback of the right inferior frontal cortex altered error-monitoring brain activation, stop-task performance, and clinical outcomes in adolescents with ADHD, compared with active-control neurofeedback of the left parahippocampal gyrus.

design.value: A single-blind randomised controlled trial comparing fMRI neurofeedback of the right inferior frontal cortex with active-control neurofeedback of the left parahippocampal gyrus, with stop-task and clinical measures collected before and after training.

description.value: Boys with ADHD who received fMRI neurofeedback of the right inferior frontal cortex.

clinical_characteristics.value: Twenty-four participants met the DSM-5 criteria for the ADHD combined hyperactive/impulsive subtype, while three met the criteria for the ADHD inattentive subtype.

medication_status.value: Fourteen rIFC-NF participants received psychostimulant medication during the study; methylphenidate: N = 12, dexamphetamine: N = 2. Two participants stopped taking their ADHD medication at least seven days before participation.

description.value: Boys with ADHD who received active-control fMRI neurofeedback of the left parahippocampal gyrus.

diagnostic_instrument.value: Schedule of Affective Disorders and Schizophrenia for School-Age Children-Present and Lifetime version (K-SADS-PL)

clinical_characteristics.value: Twenty-four participants met the DSM-5 criteria for the ADHD combined hyperactive/impulsive subtype, while three met the criteria for the ADHD inattentive subtype.

medication_status.value: Seven participants received psychostimulant medication during the study; methylphenidate: N = 7. One boy was medication-naïve and three participants stopped taking their ADHD medication at least seven days before participation.

task_description.value: The protocol consisted of four 1 h to 1.15 hr sessions within a 2-week period, totalling a maximum of 14 neurofeedback runs. Participants attempted to move a rocket toward space using feedback from the target region.

instructions.value: Participants were asked to move the rocket toward space using any strategy they could. Minimal instructions were given.

stimuli.value: A video of a rocket during activation blocks and an image of a dolphin during the initial rest block.

task_performance_measures.value: fMRI-NF performance was acquired for each run and each participant as a measure of brain regulation capacity.

task_description.value: Participants responded as fast as they could to arrows pointing left or right. In 20% of trials, a stop signal followed the go signal and participants had to inhibit their response. A tracking algorithm adjusted the interval between go and stop signals to produce 50% successful and 50% unsuccessful inhibition trials.

instructions.value: Participants were instructed to respond as fast as they could to arrows pointing left or right and to inhibit their response when a stop signal appeared.

stimuli.value: Arrows pointing left or right, followed on some trials by a stop signal.

mean reaction time to go signals
standard deviation of reaction times to go signals

description.value: Each fMRI-NF run lasted 8.5 min and consisted of 6 activation blocks of 40 s separated by rest blocks of 30 s. Feedback was updated every MRI repetition time, i.e. every 2 s.
Details of the acquisition of the fMRI Stop task can be found in Alegria et al. (2017) and in the supplementary material.
The fMRI data underwent realignment, motion correction, smoothing, global detrending and spin-excitation history correction.

model_settings.value: Individual goodness-of-fit statistic (SSQ-ratio) maps were created and transformed into standard space. The experimental condition was failed stop trials against an implicit baseline of go trials.

A repeated-measures ANOVA tested the interaction of time (pre, post) by group (rIFC-NF group, lPHG-NF group). Voxel-level threshold p < 0.05 and cluster-level threshold p < 0.02 were used, with permutation testing and cluster mass thresholding.

The fMRI-NF condition was contrasted with the baseline condition, averaged across all 11 runs. A voxel-wise test at p < 0.05 was followed by a cluster-level threshold of p < 0.011; combined voxel/cluster tests used permutation testing.
Average BOLD responses extracted from activation clusters were correlated with post-versus-pre changes in post-error reaction times and ADHD-RS clinical outcome measures in the rIFC-NF group.
